answer:
Short answer: second-hand electric, not manual — for a first machine. Manual levers (Flair NEO Flex €94, ROK €175, all new) make genuinely good espresso, but they are fiddly, single-shot, and you still need a grinder and a kettle; a lot of first-timers find the routine tiring by week three. A used Gaggia Classic gives you 58 mm standard parts, cheap spares, a steam wand and a huge mod community (PID and OPV kits), so it grows with you — and it holds value, so reselling costs you little if you quit.

Which one I'd actually buy: the Gaggia Classic Ur-Modell in Neuss at €189 (negotiable) — pre-2015 Italian build, stainless, and the seller is open to offers. If you want less risk, the £/€210 generalüberholt Vintage from a workshop is the safe version. The €200 's-Gravenhage machine is the pick if you're in NL and can collect.

One honest budget caveat: €250 does not cover machine + a grinder worth owning. If the €250 must include the grinder, buy the Flair NEO Flex at €94 (or the €100 Dedica + electric grinder bundle in Rastatt) and put the rest into a burr grinder — a mediocre grinder will ruin a Gaggia's espresso anyway.

Sites checked: kleinanzeigen.de, marktplaats.nl, idealo.de. On kleinanzeigen a dedicated "flair espresso handhebel" search returned zero hits — manual machines barely appear used there, so new via idealo is the realistic manual route. amazon.de was unusable (all sponsored ads).
